title: Normalized internal-to-section Hom and scalar comparison data
statement: Use the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $\Lambda,\Gamma$ commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], pulled back to internal rings on $X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded native derived tensor and Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], the fixed internal-to-section module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], and its termwise and derived functors $F,\Phi$ [def-sfb-internal-section-total-comparison]. Right evaluation is the native tensor-Hom counit preceded by the native braiding of [def-sfb-native-derived-koszul-braiding]. For each prescribed closed model and K-flat tensor model, a HomPresentation is a normalized TensorComparison [def-sfb-internal-section-derived-tensor-comparison] together with a natural isomorphism $\Phi H(K,L)\cong H_{\rm sec}(\Phi K,\Phi L)$ whose tensor-evaluation square commutes. The internal functorial Hom representative at a complex $P$ is $F_{\rm cpx}\circ H_{\rm rep}(F_{\rm cpx}P,-)\circ F_{\rm cpx}^{-1}$, using the whole existing representative functor [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models]; its comparison after $F_{\rm cpx}$ is the actual equivalence counit. Its localization square is the equality obtained by applying $\Phi$ to its localization map, then the HomPresentation isomorphism, endpoint localization isomorphisms, and the fixed section representative isomorphism [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. Termwise $F_{\rm cpx}$ has its inherited equivalence instance. The section-ring functor sends commutative internal rings and their maps to their actual section rings and section maps [def-sfb-section-scalar-map-data]. The canonical internal restriction compositor and unitor are the derived lifts of the actual restriction identifications, including the coefficient-functor composition and identity laws. Their left-adjoint mates, for the derived extension of scalars [def-sfb-internal-scalar-tensor-comparison] and its derived extension-restriction adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], define the internal scalar compositor and unitor [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. On the section side the scalar compositors and unitors of [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data] are transported along the actual reconstructed coefficient functor laws. All these constructions use the original extension-restriction adjunctions.
